en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.9.
Parāmāsagocchaka, Kusalattika (The Group on Grasping, Wholesome Triplet)
3.9.1. The Pair on Misapprehension (Parāmāsaduka), the Triplet on the Wholesome (Kusalattika), the Root Condition (Hetu):
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not misapprehension, a wholesome state that is not misapprehension arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, one; in the case of object condition, one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. (Abbreviated.
(In the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, it is one in every instance.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with clinging (*parāmāsa*), there arises an unwholesome state not associated with clinging by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both adherence (*parāmāsa*) and unwholesome, and a state that is not-adherence and unwholesome, there arises a state that is not-adherence and unwholesome by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). [Three.
Dependent on a state that is both adherence and unwholesome, and a state that is not-adherence and unwholesome, there arises a state that is not-adherence and unwholesome by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five; under object condition there are five ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are five. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to non-root condition: one; with respect to non-predominance: five; with respect to non-prenascence: five; with respect to non-postnascence:

five ... pe ... with respect to non-kamma: three ... pe ... with respect to non-dissociation: five. (Abbreviated. [The "Conascent Chapter" ... pe ... and the "Associated Chapter" should also be expanded.
A state that is unwholesome and not associated with lust is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is unwholesome and not associated with lust. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to root condition: three; object condition: nine; predominance condition: nine …pe… conascence, mutuality, and dependence conditions:
five; strong-dependence and repetition conditions: nine; kamma, nutriment, faculty, and jhāna conditions: three; path and association conditions:
five …pe… non-disappearance condition: five. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here.
Dependent on a non-delusive indeterminate state, a non-delusive indeterminate state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one …pe… under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-arising as well... pe ...in the section on questions as well, it is one in all cases.
3.9.2. The Dyad on the Grasped, the Triad on the Wholesome, and the Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is adhered to, a wholesome state that is adhered to arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not adhered to, a wholesome state that is not adhered to arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are two; under object condition there are two ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are two. (Abbreviated.)
(The *sahajātavāra* ... [and] the *pañhāvāra* should also be expanded in detail.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is the object of clinging, an unwholesome state that is the object of clinging arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. One [condition] under root; one under object ... [and so on] ... one under non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence, and likewise in the section on inquiry, it is the same in all cases.
Dependent on an objectified indeterminate state, an objectified indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-objectified indeterminate state, a non-objectified indeterminate state arises by way of root condition... three.

Dependent on a state that is both adhered-to and indeterminate, and a state that is not adhered-to and indeterminate, there arises a state that is adhered-to and indeterminate by way of root-condition.

(Abbreviated. Five under root; two under object ... pe ... one under repetition ... pe ... five under non-disappearance. (Abbreviated. (The "Conascent Chapter" ... pe ... and the "Investigation Chapter" should also be expanded. 3.9.3.
The Couple of Adherence-Associated States, the Triplet of Wholesome States.
Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the perversions, a wholesome state dissociated from the perversions arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there is one; under object condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-arising, and likewise in the section on questions, it is the same in all cases.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with grasping, an unwholesome state associated with grasping arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from grasping, an unwholesome state dissociated from grasping arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause, two; in the case of object, two (in all cases, two) … pe … in the case of non-disappearance, two.

(Abbreviated. In the case of not-root, one; in the case of not-predominance, two (in all cases, two) … pe … in the case of not-dissociation, two. (Abbreviated. (The section on co-nascence … pe … and the section on association should also be expanded.
An unwholesome state associated with clinging is a condition, by way of root-cause condition, for an unwholesome state associated with clinging.

An unwholesome state dissociated from the taints is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints. (Abbreviated. There are two [conditions] in the case of root;
four in the case of object; four in the case of predominance (both intermediate and final [predominances] as object-predominance);
two in the case of proximity … pe … two in the case of conascence … pe … four in the case of decisive support; two in the case of repetition; two in the case of kamma; [two] in the case of nutriment.
Two ... [and so on] ... two paths ... [and so on] ... two non-disappearances. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints of clinging and indeterminate, there arises a state dissociated from the taints of clinging and indeterminate by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, it is the same in all cases. 3.9.4.
The Dyad on Grasping and the Grasped; The Triplet on the Wholesome.
3.9.4.1.1–4. The Section on Dependent Origination, etc.
The Tetrad of Conditions:

Dependent on a wholesome state that is both "clung-to" (*parāmaṭṭha*) and not itself "clinging" (*parāmāsa*), there arises a wholesome state that is both clung-to and not clinging, by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated.
[There is] one under root, one under object ... pe ... one under non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
(Also in the section on co-nascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all cases.
Dependent on unwholesome states that are both adhered-to and adhering-to, there arises an unwholesome state that is adhered-to but not adhering-to, by way of root condition … one.
Dependent on unwholesome states that are adhered-to but not adhering-to, there arises an unwholesome state that is adhered-to but not adhering-to, by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is both a perversive adherence (*parāmāsa*) and adhered-to (*parāmaṭṭha*), and also unwholesome and adhered-to, but not itself a perversive adherence, there arises a state that is both adhered-to and not a perversive adherence, and is unwholesome, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). ... [one] ... (Abbreviated.
Under root-conditions there are five; under object-conditions there are five ... pe ... under non-disappearance conditions there are five. (Abbreviated.)
(The section on co-nascence ... and the section on association should also be expanded in detail.
An unwholesome state that is both clung-to and not itself clinging is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both clung-to and not itself clinging.
(Abbreviated. [In the root-condition there are three; in the object-condition, nine; in the predominance-condition, nine ... up to ... in the non-disappearance-condition, five. (Abbreviated.)
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here.

Dependent on a neutral state that is both clung-to (*parāmaṭṭha*) and not itself clinging (*no ca parāmāsa*), there arises a neutral state that is both clung-to and not itself clinging, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. Under root-condition: one; under object-condition (*ārammaṇa*): one ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*): one. (Abbreviated. (In the "Conascent" section ... pe ... and in the "Questions" section, it is one in every instance.)
3.9.5. The Dyad of Being Dissociated from and Grasped by the Taints (Parāmāsavippayuttaparāmaṭṭhaduka), the Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), and the Root (Hetu).

Dependent on a wholesome state that is dissociated from the taints and grasped by them, there arises a wholesome state that is dissociated from the taints and grasped by them, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the taints (*parāmāsa*) and not adhered to (*aparāmaṭṭha*), there arises a wholesome state dissociated from the taints and not adhered to, by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Two for root; two for object; ... [and so on] ... two for non-disappearance.

Dependent on an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints but adhered to, there arises an unwholesome state dissociated from the taints but adhered to, by way of root condition. (In all cases, one.)

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the perversions, grasped by them, and indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the perversions, grasped by them, and indeterminate, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the perversions, not grasped by them, and indeterminate, there arises a state that is dissociated from the perversions, not grasped by them, and indeterminate, by way of root-condition … three [cases]. Dependent on both a state that is dissociated from the perversions, grasped by them, and indeterminate, and a state that is dissociated from the perversions, not grasped by them, and indeterminate … [three cases].

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from misapprehension (*parāmāsa*), misapprehended (*parāmaṭṭha*), and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state [of the same nature] by way of the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five;
under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two ... pe ... under the repetition condition (*āsevana*) there is one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are five.
The Wholesome Triplet of the Misapprehension Group is completed.
